Difficulty not run: the submission did not pass every blocking quality or quality panel check. Oracle/NOP already passed. No Opus, GPT, analysis, or rubric-generation runs were started.

QUALITY PANEL: NEEDS REVISION -- 52 blocking issues to fix. Details for each are below.

Blocking (fix every one):
   1. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The instruction excludes binary input files by calling the
      files ASCII text, but graded fixtures contain NUL, which the governing manual expressly
      classifies as binary.
   2. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The verifier grades binary-file behavior despite the
      instruction restricting involved files to ASCII text.
   3. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The contract contradicts GNU ed and its own manual about the
      destination of the `?` error notification, requiring stdout even though the compared GNU
      run emits diagnostics on stderr.
   4. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The contract excludes binary files by limiting the files
      involved to ASCII text, but the verifier grades NUL-containing binary-file behavior.
   5. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: An unset mark resolves to an invalid address instead
      of address zero whenever the buffer is nonempty.
   6. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The bracket parser treats a leading literal hyphen as
      the start of a character range.
   7. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Looking up an unset mark incorrectly fails when the
      buffer is nonempty instead of resolving to address zero.
   8. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Resolving an unset mark walks the nonempty buffer
      looking for a nonexistent node and rejects it instead of returning address 0.
   9. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: An unset apostrophe mark is passed as a null line node
      to a lookup that rejects it when the buffer is nonempty, rather than resolving it to
      address zero.
  10. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The matcher breaks equal-length whole-match ties by
      traversal order instead of preferring the longest captured subexpression.
  11. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Continuation assembly turns a backslash-only first
      global-list line into an extra blank command, printing every selected line twice.
  12. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Mark management leaves marks attached to detached line
      nodes: substitution fails to transfer a mark to the changed line, and deletion does not
      clear the mark when the line is deleted.
  13. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Continuation parsing converts a backslash-only first
      global-list line and its following blank line into two null commands, printing every
      selected line twice.
  14. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Substitution replaces a marked line with a fresh Line
      node but leaves the mark pointing to the detached deleted node, whereas GNU ed 1.19
      preserves a mark when its line is changed.
  15. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: An apostrophe address for a never-set mark is invalid
      on a nonempty buffer instead of resolving to address 0.
  16. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The option parser accepts excluded -G and -v instead
      of accepting only the contract’s six listed options.
  17. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The `=` command accepts a syntactically parsed
      reversed address range and prints its second address instead of rejecting the invalid
      range.
  18. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Apostrophe marks do not implement GNU ed 1.19’s

  19. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: A supplied right-hand address after an omitted left
      range separator is added to the already-installed `$` endpoint instead of becoming the
      range endpoint.
  20. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Global substitution of a valid regular expression that
      matches the empty string loops at the same position and is rejected as an infinite
      substitution loop.
  21. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The reference rejects a backslash-continued
      regular-expression parameter because it parses the regexp before joining the following
      input line.
  22. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: A first global command-list line containing only a
      backslash is parsed as a line continuation rather than GNU ed 1.19's special empty list,
      so the next top-level input line is executed inside the global list.
  23. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Global substitution incorrectly treats a second
      zero-length match at the same remaining text as an infinite loop instead of advancing

  24. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The substitution parser accepts repeat-substitution

   Why this fails:

     documented binary behavior preserves its absent final newline. Flip: these cases compare
     output and written files with GNU ed at tests/test_outputs.py:133-143, so that otherwise
     contract-compliant text-only implementation fails.

     environment/app/docs/ed-errata.txt:58-61, tests/cases/fixtures.json:20-34,
     tests/cases/odd_files.jsonl:9-10, tests/test_outputs.py:133-143

   An unset mark resolves to an invalid address instead of address zero whenever the buffer is
   nonempty.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: Start with an existing file containing `a\n` and supply the regular-file command

## Quality Check Results
✅ pass - verifiable: test.sh runs pytest against test_outputs.py, which for each of 1719 committed cases spawns the image's own /usr/bin/ed (root, as oracle) and the candidate (unprivileged, via guard.py) in fresh directories with LC_ALL=C, and diffs stdout, exit status, and the resulting file tree byte-for-byte. No LLM-as-judge, no network installs at verify time (pytest/ctrf are baked into tests/Dockerfile), and the comparison is fully programmatic and deterministic given GNU ed's own determinism.
✅ pass - solvable: solution/pyed/ed.py (1426 lines) and posixre.py (333 lines) implement a complete editor model (circular line list, undo stack of add/delete/move records, address parser, POSIX leftmost-longest regex engine) whose comments explicitly track the manual and the errata file, and solve.sh copies them into /app/pyed as the delivered package. expert_time_estimate_hours=12 is on the high end of 'a few hours' but is not a multi-day effort, and a working solution is present.
✅ pass - difficult: Faithfully reproducing GNU ed 1.19 byte-for-byte requires precise handling of address arithmetic, marks, undo-of-undo, global command active-list semantics, POSIX leftmost-longest BRE/ERE matching (which Python's re does not provide), and manual/implementation divergences — this goes well beyond a standard course project and requires genuine systems/regex-engine expertise.
✅ pass - interesting: Porting a POSIX line editor to run in minimal/hardened containers that lack native `ed` (and cannot load native code) is a realistic scenario for engineers maintaining legacy shell/ed-based provisioning scripts in restricted or stdlib-only environments.
✅ pass - outcome_verified: Grading is purely on final stdout, exit status and resulting files versus the real ed oracle; the only process-level constraints (no subprocess spawn, no native code, stdlib-only) are mechanistic anti-cheat measures explicitly permitted by the rubric, not arbitrary 'use this tool' constraints.
✅ pass - anti_cheat_robustness: The agent image ships no `ed` binary at all; the verifier's real `ed` is chmod 700 before any candidate code runs; guard.py uses sys.addaudithook/meta_path to block subprocess/exec/fork/ctypes and imports from outside stdlib+delivered files, and this guard is itself exercised against five adversarial probe programs (delegate to ed, exec, ctypes/libc, vendored import, installed package) plus an AST-based audit rejecting delivered executables or foreign imports.
✅ pass - task_security: Reviewed Dockerfiles, guard.py, test.sh, and all guardcheck probes; no credential access, network exfiltration, obfuscated payloads, or prompt injection was found — probes that spawn subprocesses or load libc exist solely to validate the sandbox guard itself, not to exfiltrate anything.
✅ pass - functional_verification: Correctness is judged by actually executing both the oracle and the candidate program on identical inputs and diffing stdout/exit-status/files; the only source-level scanning (AST import check) exists to enforce the stdlib-only anti-cheat constraint, not as the primary grading mechanism.
✅ pass - deterministic_reproducible: Both Dockerfiles pin the base image by sha256 digest; pytest/pytest-json-ctrf are version-pinned; apt packages (ed, tmux, etc.) are left unpinned per accepted convention; no live services are used, and LC_ALL=C plus fixed fixtures make ed's behavior deterministic across runs.
✅ pass - essential_difficulty: The byte-exact matching requirement mirrors the task's actual goal (drop-in replacement for GNU ed), so precision is intrinsic to the problem rather than incidental formatting noise; failures would stem from genuine semantic gaps (undo, addressing, regex) rather than clerical formatting.
✅ pass - test_instruction_alignment: Every requirement enumerated in instruction.md (options -E/-l/-p/-q/-r/-s, address forms, BRE/ERE with GNU escapes, global/undo/marks/G/V, error/exit-status rules, stdlib-only/no-subprocess constraint) maps to a test family in roster.json or to the launcher/audit tests; no test introduces behavior outside what the instruction and referenced manual/errata describe.
✅ pass - novel: This is not a rote textbook exercise; it requires reconstructing GNU ed's exact internal semantics (including documented manual/implementation discrepancies in ed-errata.txt) and a leftmost-longest POSIX regex matcher, which is unlikely to be memorized verbatim from training data.
✅ pass - agentic: The agent must read the manual and errata, design and iteratively debug a multi-hundred-line editor and regex engine with no reference ed binary available in its own container, requiring exploration, testing, and multi-step iteration rather than a single-shot answer.
✅ pass - reviewable: Expected outputs are derived at verification time by running the real GNU ed 1.19 binary rather than being hardcoded, so a non-specialist reviewer can trust the oracle is 'ed itself' rather than a hand-crafted expected value; the roster/fixture consistency checks make the test corpus auditable.
✅ pass - instruction_concision: instruction.md is dense but not padded with headings, roleplay, or step-by-step how-to guidance; it uses absolute paths (/app/pyed/ed.py, /app/docs/ed.txt) and focuses on precisely scoping what must be reproduced and excluded, which is necessary content given the breadth of GNU ed's behavior rather than solution-hinting.
✅ pass - solution_quality: The reference solution is a genuine, from-scratch implementation of the editor and regex engine (not an echo of expected output), and the large source files are kept as separate files under solution/pyed/ rather than inlined heredocs in solve.sh.
✅ pass - separate_verifier_configured: artifacts=["/app/"] covers everything test_outputs.py reads (DELIVERED=/app); tests/Dockerfile bakes ed, pytest and pytest-json-ctrf with pinned versions and pre-creates /app and /logs/verifier; no runtime pip/apt installs occur in test.sh; no shared assets are duplicated across environment/ and tests/ that could drift.
✅ pass - environment_hygiene: environment/Dockerfile only COPYs app/ (stub ed.py, manual, errata, README) and installs unrelated agent tools (tmux, asciinema, patch, ca-certificates) with apt cleanup; it installs no `ed` binary and no test-only Python packages; tests/Dockerfile owns pytest/ctrf and the real ed binary with its own apt cleanup.
➖ not_applicable - structured_data_schema: The task's output is plain-text ed stdout and edited text files compared byte-for-byte against the real ed's output — there is no JSON/API/DB structured-output contract requiring a documented schema.
✅ pass - typos: Spot-checked instruction.md, task.toml, test_outputs.py, guard.py, solve.sh, and case/fixture files for common misspellings and path errors; none were found, and identifiers (family names, fixture keys, file paths) are consistent across roster.json, the .jsonl files, and test_outputs.py.
✅ pass - difficulty_explanation_quality: difficulty_explanation enumerates the concrete sources of difficulty (address/mark semantics, undo-of-undo, global active-list interaction, leftmost-longest regex, error/exit-status rules) and states the fixtures/scripts are synthetically generated for this task with expected results derived by running real GNU ed rather than stored; it stops short of an explicit one-line 'who does this job' sentence inside the field itself, though relevant_experience covers that context.
✅ pass - solution_explanation_quality: solution_explanation accurately describes the two-file port (posixre.py for backtracking leftmost-longest matching, ed.py for the circular line-list/undo-stack editor model) and is fully consistent with the actual solution source files inspected.
✅ pass - verification_explanation_quality: verification_explanation accurately describes the roster/fixture consistency check, the per-case oracle-vs-candidate run under LC_ALL=C, the guard/launcher sandboxing and its self-test probes, and the package audit — all of which match what test_outputs.py and guard.py actually implement; no inequality-based tolerances are used so no calibration justification is needed.
✅ pass - category_and_tags: category 'Software' fits a from-scratch editor/regex-engine reimplementation; subcategory 'Languages' is a reasonable fit given the command-language parsing and regex-engine implementation work; tags (gnu-ed, line-editor, posix-regex, undo, reimplementation) are specific and directly descriptive rather than generic.
✅ pass - no_extraneous_files: Every file traced to a purpose: environment/app/* is copied into the agent image and referenced by instruction.md; tests/* are all read by test_outputs.py or Dockerfile; solution/* are used by solve.sh; no stray caches, backups, or unused assets were found in the full tree listing.
✅ pass - verifier_execution_isolation: The candidate always runs under setpriv as uid 65534 through guard.py, which blocks os.fork/exec/subprocess/ctypes via sys.addaudithook and meta_path before any privileged code path is reachable; /logs/verifier and /tests are chmod 700 and the real ed binary is made root-only before candidate code runs; test.sh (root) derives the reward solely from the root pytest process's exit code, and the guard's own hardening is exercised by dedicated adversarial probe tests (exec_launcher, native ctypes, vendored import, installed package import).
✅ pass - ctrf_reporting: test.sh runs `python3 -I -m pytest ... --ctrf /logs/verifier/ctrf.json /tests/test_outputs.py -rA` directly as root, writing the CTRF report to the collected path with full per-test granularity across all 22+ test functions.
➖ not_applicable - do_not_modify_enforced: instruction.md contains no 'do not modify/preserve this artifact' style constraint on a concrete file — its only behavioral restrictions (stdlib-only, no subprocess) are process constraints already covered under anti_cheat_robustness/outcome_verified, not artifact-preservation constraints.
✅ pass - binary_reward: test.sh only ever writes literal `0` or `1` to /logs/verifier/reward.txt, initialized to 0 and set to 1 solely when the root pytest invocation's exit code is exactly 0; no fractional or weighted scoring path exists.

QUALITY PANEL: NEEDS REVISION -- 52 blocking issues to fix. Details for each are below.

Blocking (fix every one):
   1. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The instruction excludes binary input files by calling the
      files ASCII text, but graded fixtures contain NUL, which the governing manual expressly
      classifies as binary.
   2. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The verifier grades binary-file behavior despite the
      instruction restricting involved files to ASCII text.
   3. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The contract contradicts GNU ed and its own manual about the
      destination of the `?` error notification, requiring stdout even though the compared GNU
      run emits diagnostics on stderr.
   4. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The contract excludes binary files by limiting the files
      involved to ASCII text, but the verifier grades NUL-containing binary-file behavior.
   5. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: An unset mark resolves to an invalid address instead
      of address zero whenever the buffer is nonempty.
   6. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The bracket parser treats a leading literal hyphen as
      the start of a character range.
   7. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Looking up an unset mark incorrectly fails when the
      buffer is nonempty instead of resolving to address zero.
   8. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Resolving an unset mark walks the nonempty buffer
      looking for a nonexistent node and rejects it instead of returning address 0.
   9. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: An unset apostrophe mark is passed as a null line node
      to a lookup that rejects it when the buffer is nonempty, rather than resolving it to
      address zero.
  10. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The matcher breaks equal-length whole-match ties by
      traversal order instead of preferring the longest captured subexpression.
  11. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Continuation assembly turns a backslash-only first
      global-list line into an extra blank command, printing every selected line twice.
  12. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Mark management leaves marks attached to detached line
      nodes: substitution fails to transfer a mark to the changed line, and deletion does not
      clear the mark when the line is deleted.
  13. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Continuation parsing converts a backslash-only first
      global-list line and its following blank line into two null commands, printing every
      selected line twice.
  14. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Substitution replaces a marked line with a fresh Line
      node but leaves the mark pointing to the detached deleted node, whereas GNU ed 1.19
      preserves a mark when its line is changed.
  15. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: An apostrophe address for a never-set mark is invalid
      on a nonempty buffer instead of resolving to address 0.
  16. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The option parser accepts excluded -G and -v instead
      of accepting only the contract’s six listed options.

novel.explanation: While the editor-state logic in solution/pyed/ed.py mirrors GNU ed's own C algorithm structure (which a model could partially recall), the load-bearing POSIX leftmost-longest regex engine in posixre.py has no analogous reusable reference inside ed's own source (ed delegates regex matching to glibc) and must be independently designed and implemented, preventing a pure memorization shortcut for a significant fraction of the test families.

typos.explanation: No typos found in filenames, paths, commands, or identifiers across instruction.md, task.toml, Dockerfiles, solve.sh, test.sh, or the Python sources (occasional spelling like 'occurences'/'mesages' appears only inside the copied verbatim GNU ed manual text, not in task-authored content).

agentic.explanation: The agent has no ed binary and no network access to obtain one, so it must read the ~1000-line manual (/app/docs/ed.txt), iteratively author and self-test a multi-file implementation, and debug subtle edge cases across many sessions/tool-calls without an oracle to compare against — this cannot be solved by a single zero-shot generation.

solvable.explanation: solution/pyed/ed.py and posixre.py provide a complete, carefully structured implementation (buffer as linked line-nodes, undo stack, active-list global commands, a from-scratch POSIX backtracking regex engine with leftmost-longest semantics) that solve.sh installs into /app/pyed. The code is coherent, internally consistent with the manual's described behavior, and the declared 12-hour expert estimate, while above a 'few hours', is a single workday for an editor+regex-engine port, not a multi-day undertaking.

difficult.explanation: The task requires precise replication of ed's stateful current-address rules, undo-of-undo semantics, global active-list tracking, and, notably, a genuine POSIX leftmost-longest regular-expression matcher, which Python's re module does not provide and which GNU ed itself delegates to glibc rather than implementing — this sub-problem cannot be solved by simply porting ed's own C source and requires real algorithmic/regex-engine expertise.

reviewable.explanation: The verifier derives expected results by executing the actual GNU ed 1.19 binary at test time rather than hardcoding expected outputs, so a non-specialist reviewer can trust the ground truth without ed expertise; task.toml's verification_explanation matches this design precisely.

verifiable.explanation: tests/test_outputs.py runs the real /usr/bin/ed (baked into tests/Dockerfile, root-only after chmod) and the candidate /app/pyed/ed.py against 250+ scripted cases in cases.json, comparing stdout byte-for-byte, exit-status zero-ness, and final directory contents. This is fully programmatic, deterministic (no LLM-as-judge, no randomness), and requires no runtime network installs (pytest/ctrf are pip-installed at image build time in tests/Dockerfile; test.sh only runs pytest).

interesting.explanation: Providing a pure-Python, dependency-free line editor for minimal/distroless container images that still rely on ed-driven maintenance scripts is a real, if niche, systems-engineering scenario (analogous to busybox/toybox utility reimplementations for constrained environments).

binary_reward.explanation: test.sh only ever writes literal `0` or `1` to /logs/verifier/reward.txt on every reachable path (initial default 0, PWD-guard failure 0, pytest success 1, pytest failure 0); no fractional or weighted scoring exists.

task_security.explanation: No credential access, external network calls, obfuscation, or destructive operations were found in environment/Dockerfile, tests/Dockerfile, test.sh, or solve.sh; the 'r /etc/hostname' and 'w ../x.txt' test cases exercise ed's own -r restricted-mode enforcement inside ephemeral tmp directories, not real host paths outside the sandbox.

ctrf_reporting.explanation: test.sh invokes `python3 -m pytest --ctrf /logs/verifier/ctrf.json /tests/test_outputs.py -rA`, emitting a per-test CTRF report covering all 20 discrete test functions to the collected path.

outcome_verified.explanation: Grading is entirely behavioral: stdout bytes, exit status, and resulting files are compared against a live run of real GNU ed; the instruction states the end goal ('behaves exactly like GNU ed 1.19...') and does not prescribe an implementation method beyond a legitimate anti-cheat restriction (stdlib only, no subprocesses).

solution_quality.explanation: solve.sh itself only installs pre-authored files, but the referenced solution/pyed/ed.py (~500 lines) and posixre.py (~200 lines) are genuine, non-trivial, hand-authored implementations kept as separate files rather than heredocs, consistent with the accepted 'write source files that are executed' pattern.

category_and_tags.explanation: category="Software" fits a language/tool-reimplementation task; subcategory="Languages" is a reasonable, defensible fit for reimplementing an interpreter/editor's command language; tags (gnu-ed, line-editor, posix-regex, undo, reimplementation) are specific and directly descriptive of the task's skills.

environment_hygiene.explanation: environment/Dockerfile only COPYs app/ (no tests/ or solution/ leakage, reinforced by environment/.dockerignore excluding both); apt installs in both Dockerfiles are unpinned with proper update+cleanup (`rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*`); test-only pip deps (pytest, pytest-json-ctrf, pinned) live solely in tests/Dockerfile.

no_extraneous_files.explanation: Every file present (instruction.md, task.toml, environment/{Dockerfile,app/*,.dockerignore}, solution/{pyed/*,solve.sh}, tests/{Dockerfile,test.sh,test_outputs.py,cases.json}) is referenced by a Dockerfile COPY, solve.sh, or the test harness; no cruft, backups, or unused assets were found in the full directory listing.

essential_difficulty.explanation: The byte-exact output comparison mirrors ed's actual observable behavior (its own text formatting is the specification, not an arbitrary added format), so difficulty stems from correctly modeling address/undo/regex/global-command semantics rather than from artificial formatting or precision requirements.

anti_cheat_robustness.explanation: The agent's image (environment/Dockerfile) does not install the real 'ed' package and the agent has no runtime network access ([agent].network_mode = "no-network"), so it cannot obtain or shell out to a genuine ed binary to fake correctness. The ground-truth ed binary and all cases.json fixtures live solely in the verifier image, unreachable from the agent container, and are further made root-only before the candidate (demoted to uid 65534) runs.

instruction_concision.explanation: instruction.md is a short, human-sounding narrative (~12 lines), uses absolute paths and backticks for code/paths (`/app/pyed/ed.py`, `/app/docs/ed.txt`), has no headings or roleplay, and describes the required end-state and scope rather than a step-by-step implementation procedure.

do_not_modify_enforced.explanation: instruction.md contains no 'do not modify/preserve/leave unchanged' constraint naming a concrete artifact; it only restricts implementation technique (stdlib-only, no subprocess), which is not a protect-an-artifact constraint.

structured_data_schema.explanation: Output is ed's own raw byte stream (plain text), not a structured data format (JSON/CSV/schema) requiring normative documentation.

functional_verification.explanation: Verification executes both the reference ed binary and the candidate script as subprocesses on real input files and diffs actual stdout/exit-status/file-state; there is no string/keyword matching against source code anywhere in the test suite.

deterministic_reproducible.explanation: pytest==9.1.1 and pytest-json-ctrf==0.5.2 are version-pinned in tests/Dockerfile; the apt-installed 'ed' package is correctly left unpinned per apt conventions; no live external services are used; ed's command scripts and fixtures are static and non-random, so repeated runs should be consistent.

test_instruction_alignment.explanation: cases.json families (addresses, append_insert_change, substitute, global_commands, interactive_global, undo, regex/regex_extended, files_and_write, errors_and_exit, options, odd_files, mixed_scripts_1-8) map directly onto the instruction's enumerated scope; excluded features (-G, -v, h, H, shell '!') were verified absent from the test scripts, matching the instruction's stated exceptions.

separate_verifier_configured.explanation: artifacts=["/app/"] supplies /app/pyed/ed.py to the verifier; tests/Dockerfile pre-installs pytest/pytest-json-ctrf and pre-creates /app and /logs/verifier; no test.sh runtime installs occur; both Dockerfiles pin the identical base-image digest, and no shared assets diverge between environment/ and tests/.

solution_explanation_quality.explanation: solution_explanation accurately summarizes the two-file strategy (posixre.py's exhaustive leftmost-longest matcher, ed.py's linked-list/undo-stack editor model) and is fully congruent with the actual solution/pyed source files inspected.

verifier_execution_isolation.explanation: test.sh chmods /logs/verifier and /tests to 700 (root-only) before any candidate code runs; test_outputs.py executes the candidate exclusively via `setpriv --reuid=65534 --regid=65534 --clear-groups --no-new-privs` (no in-process import of agent code), captures output via communicate() with a 20s timeout and process-group SIGKILL on timeout, and root's test.sh derives the reward solely from pytest's own exit code.

difficulty_explanation_quality.explanation: The explanation concretely names the hard sub-problems (current-address tracking, undo-of-undo, global active-list semantics, interactive G/V, POSIX leftmost-longest regex vs Python's re) and states why an engineer working from memory alone gets specific details wrong; it lacks an explicit one-sentence 'who does this in real life' but the surrounding relevant_experience field and instruction context make this clear by implication.

verification_explanation_quality.explanation: verification_explanation precisely describes the differential-testing strategy (root-run reference ed vs unprivileged candidate, byte-exact stdout/exit-status/file comparisons, root-only ed binary) and matches test_outputs.py and test.sh exactly; no numeric tolerances are used, so no calibration justification is needed.

      (confirmed by running the grader)
   2. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The shown initial-file fixtures do not test loading a
      contract-legal file beyond a plausible fixed 32-line buffer.  (confirmed by running the
      grader)
   3. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: No visible case distinguishes literal unescaped braces in a basic
      regular expression from Python regex quantifier syntax.  (confirmed by running the grader)
   4. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The `f` command prints the default filename even when
      its FILE parameter sets, rather than requests printing of, that filename.
   5. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Looking up a mark that has never been set resolves its
      absent node to address zero instead of failing.
   6. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The basic-RE parser rejects a leading escaped
      interval, although the manual defines it as a literal expression.
   7. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Global substitution searches a sliced remainder as a
      new line, causing word-start assertions to match inside an existing word.
   8. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: A singleton join clears the undo stack despite being
      specified to do nothing.
   9. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: An unset mark is incorrectly resolved as address zero

  11. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: In extended-regexp mode, the parser makes `^` and `$`
      anchors even when they occur where the contract requires literal characters.
  12. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The basic-regexp parser rejects an interval escape at
      the beginning of an expression instead of interpreting it literally.
  13. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: An unset mark resolves to address zero in an empty
      buffer, allowing an addressed append that should fail.
  14. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The move-command validation uses an exclusive upper

  15. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Substitution yanks the deleted, pre-substitution line

  16. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: A substitution without a final delimiter in a nonfinal

novel.explanation: While GNU ed's source is public, reproducing its exact behavioral edge cases (POSIX leftmost-longest regex semantics that Python's re lacks, undo-of-undo, global active-list interactions) requires genuine engineering rather than recall of a memorized textbook solution; this is not a standard training-corpus exercise like FizzBuzz or sorting.

typos.explanation: No typos found in task-authored files (instruction.md, task.toml, solve.sh, test.sh, guard.py, test_outputs.py, case files). The single 'occurences' typo found is inside the verbatim upstream GNU ed manual text (environment/app/docs/ed.txt), not task-authored content.

agentic.explanation: The scope (a ~1850-line line editor plus a custom regex engine, validated only indirectly since the agent has no local ed binary or network access to check itself) cannot be produced correctly in a single zero-shot generation; it requires iterative file editing, self-testing, and debugging over many steps.

solvable.explanation: solution/pyed/ed.py and posixre.py provide a complete, structurally faithful port of GNU ed's C implementation (matching known internal function/variable names such as search_line_node, put_sbuf_line, u_current) plus an exhaustive leftmost-longest POSIX regex engine. solve.sh simply installs these pre-written files. Given expert_time_estimate_hours=12 and the size/fidelity of the port, this is achievable by an expert already familiar with ed's algorithm, though it is on the high end of 'a few hours'.

difficult.explanation: Requires precise knowledge of ed's undo/redo semantics, global-active-list bookkeeping, current-address rules after every command, POSIX BRE/ERE leftmost-longest matching (which Python's re does not implement), and error/exit-status edge cases. This goes well beyond a typical undergraduate exercise and matches the stated difficulty_explanation.

reviewable.explanation: Expected outputs are not hardcoded; they are derived at verification time by running the actual GNU ed 1.19 binary, so a non-specialist reviewer can trust the oracle without independently verifying ed semantics. The verification_explanation and difficulty_explanation document the design (roster/fixture self-check, launcher probes) clearly enough for review.

verifiable.explanation: test_outputs.py deterministically runs GNU ed 1.19 (baked into tests/Dockerfile) and the candidate through a launcher, in fresh temp dirs, comparing stdout byte-for-byte, exit status, and resulting files. No LLM-as-judge, no runtime network installs in test.sh (all verifier tooling - pytest, pytest-json-ctrf, ed - is baked into tests/Dockerfile). The roster/fixtures self-check (load_cases) guards against silent corpus drift.

interesting.explanation: Reimplementing a standard POSIX utility for minimal/distroless container images is a realistic professional scenario (embedded/minimal-image maintenance, script portability); the relevant_experience field plausibly identifies the audience (Unix systems engineers maintaining ed/sed scripts).

binary_reward.explanation: test.sh writes exactly 0 initially, then unconditionally overwrites reward.txt with either '1' (rc==0) or '0' (rc!=0) based solely on pytest's exit code; every reachable path writes exactly 0 or 1, with no fractional or weighted scoring anywhere in the verifier.

task_security.explanation: No credential access, no exfiltration, no obfuscation. The guardcheck probes intentionally attempt subprocess/exec/ctypes usage purely to test the anti-cheat guard, which is the guard's own documented purpose. One case reads /etc/hostname via ed's 'r' command, which is benign (compared identically between reference and candidate, no external transmission).

ctrf_reporting.explanation: test.sh invokes pytest with --ctrf /logs/verifier/ctrf.json directly against test_outputs.py, covering its 24 discrete tests (22 case-family tests plus the two guard/package tests), matching the standard CTRF pattern exactly.

outcome_verified.explanation: Tests only check final stdout, exit status, and resulting files against a live GNU ed run; instructions describe required behavior/output, not an implementation approach. No process-level constraints on how the agent must implement pyed.

solution_quality.explanation: solve.sh only copies pre-written solution/pyed/ed.py and posixre.py (each far over 20 lines) rather than inlining them as heredocs, matching the guidance to keep large files separate. The files themselves demonstrate genuine, non-trivial computation (a full editor engine and regex matcher), not a hardcoded answer.

category_and_tags.explanation: category='Software' and subcategory='Languages' reasonably fit a task about implementing a command-language interpreter and its own regex dialect. Tags (gnu-ed, line-editor, posix-regex, undo, reimplementation) are specific and descriptive, not generic.

environment_hygiene.explanation: environment/Dockerfile only COPYs app/ (README, docs, pyed stub); tests/ and solution/ are excluded via .dockerignore and never copied. tests/Dockerfile installs its own test-only deps (ed, pytest, pytest-json-ctrf) at build time, not in test.sh. Apt installs in both Dockerfiles are unpinned (correct per guidance) and followed by rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* cleanup, preceded by apt-get update.

no_extraneous_files.explanation: Every file inspected is referenced by a Dockerfile, the instruction, solve.sh, or the test harness (roster.json/fixtures.json cross-checked against the *.jsonl case files and found perfectly consistent, with fixture and total counts matching exactly). No leftover, backup, or unused files were found; the only hidden file is the standard .dockerignore.

essential_difficulty.explanation: The byte-exact output requirement is intrinsic to faithfully cloning GNU ed's documented behavior (e.g. the 'l' command's escaping rules, diagnostic messages), not an arbitrary formatting overlay bolted onto an otherwise different task. Failures would stem from misunderstanding ed's genuine semantics (current-address rules, undo, leftmost-longest matching), not clerical precision.

anti_cheat_robustness.explanation: The agent image ships no ed binary and has no network at solve time (agent network_mode=no-network), preventing trivial delegation. The guard.py launcher uses sys.addaudithook and a meta_path Warden to block subprocess/exec/fork/ctypes and non-stdlib/non-delivered imports, verified against five probe programs (launcher.py, exec_launcher.py, vendored.py, native.py, plain.py). test_delivered_package_is_standard_library_python additionally scans all delivered files for binary/native content and disallowed imports via AST, closing the loophole of dropping a compiled .so under /app. Ground truth is produced live from the verifier's own root-only /usr/bin/ed, never exposed to the agent.

instruction_concision.explanation: instruction.md is dense but purely descriptive of required behavior (uses absolute paths /app/pyed/ed.py, /app/docs/ed.txt; backticks for commands/paths; no headings, roleplay, or step-by-step procedure). It does not hint at implementation approach (no mention of linked lists, undo stacks, etc.).

do_not_modify_enforced.explanation: instruction.md contains no 'do not modify/preserve/leave unchanged' constraint naming a concrete artifact; its behavioral constraints (stdlib-only, no subprocess, no native code) are enforced by the guard/launcher and delivered-package tests but are not 'do-not-modify-a-file' constraints in the sense this criterion targets.

structured_data_schema.explanation: The task's expected output is plain stdout/file content matching GNU ed's behavior, not a structured schema like JSON/CSV/API response, so no normative schema documentation is needed.

functional_verification.explanation: The core verification (check()) executes both GNU ed and the candidate on 1644 real command scripts and diffs stdout/exit-status/files. The only string/AST-based checks (test_delivered_package_is_standard_library_python) validate the 'stdlib-only, no native code' constraint, which cannot be checked by execution alone and is a legitimate complement, not a substitute, for behavioral testing.

deterministic_reproducible.explanation: Base images pinned by sha256 digest; pytest and pytest-json-ctrf pinned to exact versions; apt-get ed is intentionally left unpinned per guidance (apt mirrors only carry current point releases). No live/mutable network services are used at verify time (network_mode=no-network for both agent and verifier).

test_instruction_alignment.explanation: Every requirement in instruction.md (options -E/-l/-p/-q/-r/-s and no others, address forms, BRE/ERE with GNU escapes, leftmost-longest matching, all other commands/suffixes/global/undo/marks/G/V, error '?' + stop-on-regular-file/continue-on-pipe behavior) is covered by a corresponding case family or the launcher/package tests. Verified absence of excluded features (h/H commands, -G/-v options, '!' usage) in the corpus, matching the instruction's stated exceptions.

separate_verifier_configured.explanation: All verifier inputs (case corpus, guard/guardcheck/guardvendor, GNU ed binary, pytest/ctrf tooling) are baked into tests/Dockerfile; nothing is read from undeclared agent-container paths. No runtime pip/apt installs occur in test.sh. There are no shared assets duplicated between environment/ and tests/ that could drift.

solution_explanation_quality.explanation: solution_explanation accurately describes the two-file approach (posixre.py for BRE/ERE parsing and exhaustive leftmost-longest matching; ed.py for the circular line-list/undo-stack port) and is fully consistent with the actual solution files inspected.

verifier_execution_isolation.explanation: Candidate code always runs via setpriv --reuid=65534 (nobody), never as root, and never in-process inside pytest (always via subprocess.Popen). /logs/verifier and /tests are chmod 700 and the reference ed binary is chmod 700 before any candidate code runs. Reward is derived by root (test.sh) purely from pytest's exit code. The audit-hook guard blocks fork/exec/spawn outright, closing the double-fork-daemon attack this criterion targets; timeouts kill the whole process group via killpg with start_new_session=True.

difficulty_explanation_quality.explanation: difficulty_explanation concretely enumerates the specific hard sub-problems (current-address rules, undo-of-undo, global active-list semantics, interactive G/V, leftmost-longest POSIX matching, error/exit-status nuances) and explains why an engineer working from memory would get specific details wrong. It also clarifies the corpus is synthetically generated from the grammar rather than an external corpus, addressing the data-realism requirement. The real-world audience is covered via the closely related relevant_experience field rather than embedded verbatim in difficulty_explanation, a minor stylistic gap.

verification_explanation_quality.explanation: verification_explanation accurately and specifically describes the verifier's mechanics (roster/fixture self-check, live GNU ed oracle per case, root-only ed binary, unprivileged launcher-wrapped candidate run, byte-for-byte/exit-status/file comparison, five guard probes, delivered-package stdlib/text check), all of which match what was found in test_outputs.py and guard.py.

Its global substitution loop, however, passes each unconsumed suffix of a line to a new regex search. Word-boundary assertions then see that suffix as the beginning of a word rather than retaining their position in the addressed line. This changes both substitution output and, in some cases, whether a command succeeds.

  [part 3 of 10] The address, option, comment and prompt paths in this part implement their stated rules. A boundary between the join and undo rules does not: a one-line join correctly leaves the buffer unchanged, but discards the undo history of the preceding modification. A subsequent u therefore fails instead of undoing that modification.

An unset mark is mishandled specifically in an empty buffer: the reference converts it to address zero, so a command that should fail instead prints a value and exits successfully.

novel.explanation: This is not a rote textbook exercise; it requires reconstructing GNU ed's exact internal semantics (including documented manual/implementation discrepancies in ed-errata.txt) and a leftmost-longest POSIX regex matcher, which is unlikely to be memorized verbatim from training data.

typos.explanation: Spot-checked instruction.md, task.toml, test_outputs.py, guard.py, solve.sh, and case/fixture files for common misspellings and path errors; none were found, and identifiers (family names, fixture keys, file paths) are consistent across roster.json, the .jsonl files, and test_outputs.py.

agentic.explanation: The agent must read the manual and errata, design and iteratively debug a multi-hundred-line editor and regex engine with no reference ed binary available in its own container, requiring exploration, testing, and multi-step iteration rather than a single-shot answer.

solvable.explanation: solution/pyed/ed.py (1426 lines) and posixre.py (333 lines) implement a complete editor model (circular line list, undo stack of add/delete/move records, address parser, POSIX leftmost-longest regex engine) whose comments explicitly track the manual and the errata file, and solve.sh copies them into /app/pyed as the delivered package. expert_time_estimate_hours=12 is on the high end of 'a few hours' but is not a multi-day effort, and a working solution is present.

difficult.explanation: Faithfully reproducing GNU ed 1.19 byte-for-byte requires precise handling of address arithmetic, marks, undo-of-undo, global command active-list semantics, POSIX leftmost-longest BRE/ERE matching (which Python's re does not provide), and manual/implementation divergences — this goes well beyond a standard course project and requires genuine systems/regex-engine expertise.

reviewable.explanation: Expected outputs are derived at verification time by running the real GNU ed 1.19 binary rather than being hardcoded, so a non-specialist reviewer can trust the oracle is 'ed itself' rather than a hand-crafted expected value; the roster/fixture consistency checks make the test corpus auditable.

verifiable.explanation: test.sh runs pytest against test_outputs.py, which for each of 1719 committed cases spawns the image's own /usr/bin/ed (root, as oracle) and the candidate (unprivileged, via guard.py) in fresh directories with LC_ALL=C, and diffs stdout, exit status, and the resulting file tree byte-for-byte. No LLM-as-judge, no network installs at verify time (pytest/ctrf are baked into tests/Dockerfile), and the comparison is fully programmatic and deterministic given GNU ed's own determinism.

interesting.explanation: Porting a POSIX line editor to run in minimal/hardened containers that lack native `ed` (and cannot load native code) is a realistic scenario for engineers maintaining legacy shell/ed-based provisioning scripts in restricted or stdlib-only environments.

binary_reward.explanation: test.sh only ever writes literal `0` or `1` to /logs/verifier/reward.txt, initialized to 0 and set to 1 solely when the root pytest invocation's exit code is exactly 0; no fractional or weighted scoring path exists.

task_security.explanation: Reviewed Dockerfiles, guard.py, test.sh, and all guardcheck probes; no credential access, network exfiltration, obfuscated payloads, or prompt injection was found — probes that spawn subprocesses or load libc exist solely to validate the sandbox guard itself, not to exfiltrate anything.

ctrf_reporting.explanation: test.sh runs `python3 -I -m pytest ... --ctrf /logs/verifier/ctrf.json /tests/test_outputs.py -rA` directly as root, writing the CTRF report to the collected path with full per-test granularity across all 22+ test functions.

outcome_verified.explanation: Grading is purely on final stdout, exit status and resulting files versus the real ed oracle; the only process-level constraints (no subprocess spawn, no native code, stdlib-only) are mechanistic anti-cheat measures explicitly permitted by the rubric, not arbitrary 'use this tool' constraints.

solution_quality.explanation: The reference solution is a genuine, from-scratch implementation of the editor and regex engine (not an echo of expected output), and the large source files are kept as separate files under solution/pyed/ rather than inlined heredocs in solve.sh.

category_and_tags.explanation: category 'Software' fits a from-scratch editor/regex-engine reimplementation; subcategory 'Languages' is a reasonable fit given the command-language parsing and regex-engine implementation work; tags (gnu-ed, line-editor, posix-regex, undo, reimplementation) are specific and directly descriptive rather than generic.

environment_hygiene.explanation: environment/Dockerfile only COPYs app/ (stub ed.py, manual, errata, README) and installs unrelated agent tools (tmux, asciinema, patch, ca-certificates) with apt cleanup; it installs no `ed` binary and no test-only Python packages; tests/Dockerfile owns pytest/ctrf and the real ed binary with its own apt cleanup.

no_extraneous_files.explanation: Every file traced to a purpose: environment/app/* is copied into the agent image and referenced by instruction.md; tests/* are all read by test_outputs.py or Dockerfile; solution/* are used by solve.sh; no stray caches, backups, or unused assets were found in the full tree listing.

essential_difficulty.explanation: The byte-exact matching requirement mirrors the task's actual goal (drop-in replacement for GNU ed), so precision is intrinsic to the problem rather than incidental formatting noise; failures would stem from genuine semantic gaps (undo, addressing, regex) rather than clerical formatting.

anti_cheat_robustness.explanation: The agent image ships no `ed` binary at all; the verifier's real `ed` is chmod 700 before any candidate code runs; guard.py uses sys.addaudithook/meta_path to block subprocess/exec/fork/ctypes and imports from outside stdlib+delivered files, and this guard is itself exercised against five adversarial probe programs (delegate to ed, exec, ctypes/libc, vendored import, installed package) plus an AST-based audit rejecting delivered executables or foreign imports.

instruction_concision.explanation: instruction.md is dense but not padded with headings, roleplay, or step-by-step how-to guidance; it uses absolute paths (/app/pyed/ed.py, /app/docs/ed.txt) and focuses on precisely scoping what must be reproduced and excluded, which is necessary content given the breadth of GNU ed's behavior rather than solution-hinting.

do_not_modify_enforced.explanation: instruction.md contains no 'do not modify/preserve this artifact' style constraint on a concrete file — its only behavioral restrictions (stdlib-only, no subprocess) are process constraints already covered under anti_cheat_robustness/outcome_verified, not artifact-preservation constraints.

structured_data_schema.explanation: The task's output is plain-text ed stdout and edited text files compared byte-for-byte against the real ed's output — there is no JSON/API/DB structured-output contract requiring a documented schema.

functional_verification.explanation: Correctness is judged by actually executing both the oracle and the candidate program on identical inputs and diffing stdout/exit-status/files; the only source-level scanning (AST import check) exists to enforce the stdlib-only anti-cheat constraint, not as the primary grading mechanism.

deterministic_reproducible.explanation: Both Dockerfiles pin the base image by sha256 digest; pytest/pytest-json-ctrf are version-pinned; apt packages (ed, tmux, etc.) are left unpinned per accepted convention; no live services are used, and LC_ALL=C plus fixed fixtures make ed's behavior deterministic across runs.

I reviewed my prompt (instruction.md) and:

  • Ensured it does not list an excessive number of requirements (20+)
  • Made it sound natural and human

fields.label: Quality Judge Panel Feedback
fields.description:
After initial submission, you will be provided with detailed feedback along 5 axes, each answering a core question about your task:

  1. Coherent Contracts: Can a candidate determine every rule used to grade the task?
  2. Correct Reference Solution: Does the reference satisfy the documented task?
  3. Protected Ground Truth: Can candidate code obtain or control the answer the grader trusts?
  4. Sound Verifier: Does grading reject wrong solutions and accept contract-valid ones?
  5. Deterministic Execution: Does the same submission receive stable grading on repeated runs?

Keep these in mind when reviewing this feedback, and refer to the guidelines for more details on this feedback.
